name: aws_iam_role
description: Provides an IAM role resource. IAM roles are identities you can create in AWS that have specific permissions. A role does not have standard long-term credentials such as a password or access keys associated with it. Instead, when you assume a role, it provides temporary security credentials for your role session. IAM roles are essential for EKS node groups, ECS task execution, Lambda functions, and service-to-service communication.
use_cases: Grant EC2/EKS nodes permissions to call AWS services
ECS task execution role for pulling container images and writing logs
Lambda function execution with specific service permissions
Service accounts for Kubernetes pods (via IRSA for EKS)

required.name: assume_role_policy
required.description: The policy that grants an entity permission to assume the role. This is a JSON string defining who can assume the role (the trust relationship).

optional.name: name
optional.description: The name of the role. If omitted, Terraform will assign a random unique name.

optional.name: description
optional.description: Description of the role. Max 1000 characters.

optional.name: max_session_duration
optional.description: Maximum session duration in seconds (between 3600 and 43200). Defaults to 3600.

optional.name: path
optional.description: Path in IAM namespace. Defaults to '/'.

optional.name: permissions_boundary
optional.description: ARN of the policy used as permissions boundary. Limits maximum permissions for the role.

optional.name: tags
optional.description: Map of tags to assign to the role.

best_practices: Use jsonencode() for assume_role_policy instead of raw JSON strings
Apply the principle of least privilege — grant only the minimum permissions required
Use aws_iam_role_policy_attachment with managed policies when possible
Use aws_iam_role_policy for inline policies that are specific to the role
Tag roles for cost allocation and auditing
Use IAM Roles for Service Accounts (IRSA) for Kubernetes pods instead of node-level permissions
Set descriptive names that include the service and environment
Use permissions boundaries for delegated role creation
security_notes: Never use wildcard (*) actions or resources in production — always scope to specific services/ARNs
Use IAM Access Analyzer to identify unused permissions and external access
Enable CloudTrail to log all IAM API calls
Use IRSA (IAM Roles for Service Accounts) for pod-level permissions in EKS
Rotate credentials regularly and use temporary credentials (STS) over long-term access keys
Never embed AWS credentials in Terraform files or application code

common_errors.error: InvalidClientTokenId: The security token included in the request is invalid
common_errors.fix: Check that the trust relationship (assume_role_policy) correctly references the service or principal

common_errors.error: AccessDenied when EKS nodes cannot join cluster
common_errors.fix: Ensure AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy, AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy, and AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly are attached
IAM role names must be unique within an AWS account — use a unique naming convention with project and environment
